items.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998
items.q: Oh they’re great players. No, no, no, those are great players.

ctx.x: It’s in decay. It’s pop and rock. Not even pop, it’s rock & roll. It’s not even rock & roll it’s — I don’t know what you call it because I don’t listen to it. It’s sickening. It’s noise. Noise is the way I describe it. But of course I’m an old reprobate.
What about fellows like Warren Vache, Scott Hamilton?

Oh they’re great players. No, no, no, those are great players. I love Dixieland. You know you have Dixieland, you have traditional music, you have some of the greatest jazz musicians in the world play here at Hamilton. You know, Warren Vache, you have Kenny Davern, you have, name them, Ralph Sutton.
